title: Use Percent to Solve Problems
contentObjective: I can solve problems involving discounts, markups, tax, and tips using percents.
languageObjective: I can explain my solution using the words discount, markup, tax, tip, and percent.

noticeAndWonder.context: Before you head to the arcade prize shop to work out discounts and tax, warm up with a percent problem. Three hundred middle school students voted for one of three snacks to add to the school cafeteria menu. The graph shows the percentage of students who voted for each snack. How many students voted for fruit?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Book Fair
revealWordProblem.text: Students were asked which night of the book fair they planned to attend. The results of the survey are shown. Twenty percent of the students who planned to attend on Wednesday attended on Thursday instead. Twenty-five percent of the students who planned to attend on Thursday attended on Friday instead. Which day, Thursday or Friday, had a greater actual attendance? How many more students attended that day?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The survey shows 70 students planned for Wednesday, 112 for Thursday, and 65 for Friday. 20% of the 70 Wednesday planners moved to Thursday: 0.20 × 70 = 14 students. 25% of the 112 Thursday planners moved to Friday: 0.25 × 112 = 28 students. Actual Thursday attendance = 112 − 28 + 14 = 98. Actual Friday attendance = 65 + 28 = 93. Thursday had greater actual attendance, by 98 − 93 = 5 students.

launch.narrative: Welcome to the arcade prize shop! You've been saving up tickets and now it's time to spend them. Some prizes are on sale with discounts, but the shop also charges a 5% ticket tax on purchases. Plus, there's a 10% markup on limited-edition prizes. Can you figure out the final ticket cost for each prize?
launch.contextImage: Arcade prize counter with stuffed animals and electronics showing price tags with discount and tax labels
noticePrompts: What happens to the price when there is a discount?
What happens to the price when tax is added?
wonderPrompts: Does it matter whether you apply the discount or tax first?
How do you find the total cost after both a discount and a tax?

conceptIntro.heading: How do I find a price after a discount and then a tax?
conceptIntro.intro: A discount lowers a price. A tax, tip, or markup raises a price. Each one is a percent of the price.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Take the discount off first to get the new lower price, then add the tax on that new price.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: A bear costs 200 tickets, 25% off, then a 5% tax is added.
First the discount: 0.25 × 200 = 50 off, so the price is 200 − 50 = 150.
Then the tax on the new price: 0.05 × 150 = 7.5.
I add it on: 150 + 7.5 = 157.5 tickets is the final price.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A keychain costs 80 tickets with 10% off, then 5% tax.
What is 10% of 80, and what is the price after the discount? (8 off, so 72)
Now find 5% tax on 72 and add it. What is the final price? (3.6 tax, total 75.6)

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the table, find the discount, the price after discount, the tax, and the final price.
Always take the discount first, then add the tax.

optional.stem: Store 1 — Sneaker Spot: A pair of sneakers is $60 with 20% off. What is the sale price?
choiceFeedback: Find 20% of $60, then subtract.
Calculate discount.
That is how much you save, not how much you pay. Take that savings off the original $60 to finish the problem.
optional.stemEs: Tienda 1 — Sneaker Spot: Un par de tenis cuesta $60 con 20% de descuento. ¿Cuál es el precio de oferta?
hints: A discount comes off the original price, so the sale price has to be less than $60.
First find how much 20% of $60 is, then subtract that savings from the original price.
Write 20% as 0.20 and multiply: 0.20 × 60. Once you have that discount amount, take it away from $60.
hintsEs: Un descuento se quita del precio original, así que el precio de oferta tiene que ser menor que $60.
Primero halla cuánto es el 20% de $60 y luego resta ese ahorro del precio original.
Escribe 20% como 0.20 y multiplica: 0.20 × 60. Cuando tengas esa cantidad de descuento, réstala de $60.

optional.stem: Store 2 — Tech Stop: A $25 phone case has 8% sales tax added. What is the total cost?
choiceFeedback: Find 8% of $25 and add.
Calculate tax.
Sales tax gets added to the price, not taken off it. Find 8% of $25, then add it to the original cost.
optional.stemEs: Tienda 2 — Tech Stop: Una funda para teléfono de $25 tiene un impuesto sobre la venta del 8%. ¿Cuál es el costo total?
hints: Sales tax is an extra amount added on top of the price, so the total has to be more than $25.
Find 8% of $25 first, then add that tax to the original price.
Write 8% as 0.08 and multiply: 0.08 × 25. Then add that tax amount onto the $25.
hintsEs: El impuesto sobre la venta es una cantidad adicional que se agrega al precio, así que el total tiene que ser mayor que $25.
Primero halla el 8% de $25 y luego suma ese impuesto al precio original.
Escribe 8% como 0.08 y multiplica: 0.08 × 25. Después suma esa cantidad de impuesto a los $25.

optional.stem: Store 3 — Food Court: Your lunch bill is $40. You leave a 15% tip. How much is the tip?
choiceFeedback: Find 15% of $40 and add.
Calculate tip.
That is what you would pay in all, but the question asks only for the tip. Stop once you have found the percent of the bill.
optional.stemEs: Tienda 3 — Food Court: Tu cuenta del almuerzo es de $40. Dejas una propina del 15%. ¿De cuánto es la propina?
hints: The question asks for the tip by itself, not the total amount you hand over.
Find 15% of the $40 bill by writing the percent as a decimal and multiplying.
Set up 0.15 × 40. You can also think of it as 10% of $40 plus half of that amount — finish the calculation from there.
hintsEs: La pregunta pide solo la propina, no la cantidad total que entregas.
Halla el 15% de la cuenta de $40 escribiendo el porcentaje como decimal y multiplicando.
Plantea 0.15 × 40. También puedes pensarlo como el 10% de $40 más la mitad de esa cantidad — termina el cálculo desde ahí.

optional.instructions: Store 4 — Deal Sorter: Sort each mall sign by what it does to the final price.

items.text: Store adds a 12% markup on collectibles

optional.explanation: Three signs remove money from the price: 35% off backpacks, the 50% off clearance on shoes, and the 15% off coupon. Three signs add money on top: the 7% sales tax at checkout, the 18% tip at the smoothie bar, and the 12% markup on collectibles. You do not need the actual prices — the words "off" and "coupon" point down, while "tax," "tip," and "markup" point up.
optional.explanationEs: Tres letreros quitan dinero del precio: 35 % de descuento en mochilas, la liquidación de 50 % en zapatos y el cupón de 15 %. Tres letreros agregan dinero: el impuesto de venta del 7 % en la caja, la propina del 18 % en la barra de smoothies y el aumento del 12 % en los coleccionables. No necesitas los precios reales: las palabras "off" y "cupón" apuntan hacia abajo, mientras que "impuesto", "propina" y "aumento" apuntan hacia arriba.
hints: Every sign is either taking part of the price away or piling something extra on top — decide which one before you look at the number.
Sort by the key word: "off," "clearance," and "coupon" lower the price, while "tax," "tip," and "markup" raise it.
Start with "7% sales tax at checkout": tax is charged in addition to what the item costs, so ask whether that makes you hand over more money or less.
hintsEs: Cada letrero quita parte del precio o le agrega algo extra: decide cuál de las dos antes de mirar el número.
Clasifica por la palabra clave: "off", "liquidación" y "cupón" bajan el precio, mientras que "impuesto", "propina" y "aumento" lo suben.
Empieza con "7% sales tax at checkout": el impuesto se cobra además de lo que cuesta el artículo, así que pregúntate si eso hace que pagues más o menos.
optional.instructionsEs: Tienda 4 — Clasificador de ofertas: Clasifica cada letrero del centro comercial según lo que le hace al precio final.

optional.label: Store 5 — Price Match: Match each mall purchase to its correct final price.
optional.explanation: Two of these take money off and two add it on. The $100 jacket at 30% off loses $30, leaving $70, and the $80 boots at 25% off lose $20, leaving $60. The $50 game with 10% tax gains $5 for a total of $55, and the $20 meal with a 25% tip gains $5 for a total of $25. Deciding up or down first cuts the choices in half before you compute.
optional.explanationEs: Dos de estos quitan dinero y dos lo agregan. La chamarra de $100 con 30 % de descuento pierde $30 y queda en $70, y las botas de $80 con 25 % de descuento pierden $20 y quedan en $60. El juego de $50 con 10 % de impuesto gana $5 para un total de $55, y la comida de $20 con 25 % de propina gana $5 para un total de $25. Decidir primero si sube o baja reduce las opciones a la mitad antes de calcular.
hints: Read each purchase for the word "off" versus "added" — a discount card can never match a price larger than the one it started with.
Find the percent amount first, then subtract it for a discount or add it for tax or a tip, and look for that total on the right.
Take "$80 boots, 25% off": 25% is one fourth, so divide 80 by 4 to find the amount saved — then subtract it to see which card fits.
hintsEs: Lee cada compra buscando la palabra "off" o "added": una tarjeta con descuento nunca puede corresponder a un precio mayor que el de partida.
Encuentra primero la cantidad del porcentaje, luego réstala si es descuento o súmala si es impuesto o propina, y busca ese total a la derecha.
Toma "$80 boots, 25% off": 25 % es una cuarta parte, así que divide 80 entre 4 para hallar lo que ahorras y luego réstalo para ver qué tarjeta corresponde.
optional.labelEs: Tienda 5 — Precio correcto: Une cada compra del centro comercial con su precio final correcto.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Tax-on-Discounted-Price Mistake

workedExample.label: A $90 hoodie is 20% off, then 6% tax is added. Find the final price.
Find the discount and the sale price

optional.correctWork: Tax must be charged on the price you actually pay ($72), not the original $90. Tax = 0.06 x 72 = 4.32. Final price = 72 + 4.32 = $76.32.
hints: After a discount, you pay the lower sale price. Which price should the tax be based on?
Tax should be 0.06 x 72 = 4.32, not 0.06 x 90. Final price: 72 + 4.32 = $76.32.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Error del impuesto sobre el precio con descuento
optional.explanation: The discount was handled correctly, giving a sale price of 90 − 18 = $72. The "Add the tax" step is where it breaks: the 6% was charged on the original $90 instead of on the $72 you actually pay. Tax = 0.06 × 72 = $4.32, so the final price is 72 + 4.32 = $76.32, not $77.40.
optional.explanationEs: El descuento se hizo bien y dio un precio de oferta de 90 − 18 = $72. El paso "Add the tax" es donde falla: el 6 % se cobró sobre los $90 originales en lugar de sobre los $72 que realmente pagas. Impuesto = 0.06 × 72 = $4.32, así que el precio final es 72 + 4.32 = $76.32, no $77.40.

approaching.stem: A prize costs 120 tickets and is 25% off. What is the sale price?
choiceFeedback: Find 25% of 120, then subtract from the original.
Calculate the discount, then find what's left.
Check: 25% of 120 is how much off?
hints: '25% off' means the discount gets SUBTRACTED — the sale price must be less than 120 tickets.
Two steps: find 25% of 120 first, then subtract that discount from 120.
Start with the discount: 0.25 × 120 (or 120 ÷ 4, since 25% is one-fourth). Then take it off the 120.
approaching.stemEs: Un premio cuesta 120 boletos y tiene 25% de descuento. ¿Cuál es el precio de oferta?

approaching.stem: A meal costs $20. You leave a 15% tip. How much is the tip?
choiceFeedback: Multiply $20 by 0.15 to find the tip amount.
Find 15% of $20.
Check your calculation of the tip.
hints: The question only asks for the TIP amount — not the meal plus the tip.
The tip is 15% of the $20 bill: convert 15% to a decimal and multiply.
Set up 0.15 × 20. (Shortcut: 10% of $20 is $2, and 5% is half of that — add them.)
approaching.stemEs: Una comida cuesta $20. Dejas una propina del 15%. ¿De cuánto es la propina?

approaching.stem: A shirt costs $40 and the sales tax is 5%. What is the total cost including tax?
choiceFeedback: Find 5% of $40 and add to the price.
Calculate the tax and add to find the total cost.
Check: what is 5% of $40?
hints: Tax gets ADDED on, so the total must be a little more than $40.
Two steps: find 5% of $40 for the tax, then add it to the $40 price.
Start with the tax: 0.05 × 40. Then add that amount onto $40.
approaching.stemEs: Una camisa cuesta $40 y el impuesto sobre la venta es del 5%. ¿Cuál es el costo total con impuesto?

approaching.stem: A game originally costs 200 tickets. It is marked up 10%. What is the new price?
choiceFeedback: Find 10% of 200 and add to the original.
Calculate the markup and add to find the new price.
Check: what is 10% more than 200?
hints: 'Marked up' means the price goes UP — the new price must be more than 200 tickets.
Find 10% of 200 first, then add it to the original price.
Use the 10% shortcut: slide the decimal in 200 one place left to get the markup, then add it to 200.
approaching.stemEs: Un juego cuesta originalmente 200 boletos. Se le aplica un aumento del 10%. ¿Cuál es el precio nuevo?

approaching.instructions: Sort each situation: does the final price go UP or DOWN?
hints: Focus on what each word DOES to the price: some words take money off, others add money on.
Discounts and '% off' sales lower the price. Tax, tips, and markups add to it.
Try '20% discount on a jacket' first: a discount takes money off, so the price goes DOWN. Test each card's key word the same way.
approaching.explanation: The key word in each card tells you the direction. A 20% discount, a 30% off clearance sale, and buy-one-get-one 50% off all take part of the price away, so the final price goes down. Sales tax, a tip, and a store markup are all amounts added on top of the price you started with, so those go up.
approaching.explanationEs: La palabra clave de cada tarjeta te dice la dirección. Un descuento del 20 %, una liquidación con 30 % de rebaja y la promoción de 50 % de descuento en la segunda pieza quitan parte del precio, así que el precio final baja. El impuesto sobre la venta, la propina y el aumento que pone la tienda son cantidades que se agregan al precio inicial, así que suben.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada situación: ¿el precio final SUBE o BAJA?

approaching.title: Spot the Tip Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: A meal costs $20 and you leave a 10% tip. Find the total you pay.

workedExample.label: Find the total
workedExample.work: The student wrote the total as $2.

approaching.correctWork: $2 is only the tip, not the total. A tip is added on top of the bill: $20 + $2 = $22 total.
hints: Did the student stop after finding just the tip amount?
A tip is added to the bill: $20 + $2 = $22 total.
approaching.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la propina
approaching.explanation: The tip itself was found correctly: 0.10 × 20 = $2. The mistake is in the "Find the total" step, where $2 is reported as the total. A tip is added on top of the bill, so the total is $20 + $2 = $22 — and $2 could never be the total, since it is less than the meal itself.
approaching.explanationEs: La propina se calculó bien: 0.10 × 20 = $2. El error está en el paso "Find the total", donde se reporta $2 como el total. La propina se agrega sobre la cuenta, así que el total es $20 + $2 = $22; además, $2 nunca podría ser el total, porque es menos que la comida misma.

rows: A $45 game has a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
A $60 controller has 8% tax. What is the total?
A $25 meal with 15% tip. What is the total?
hints: The Calculation column already sets up each problem — the parentheses part is the discount, tax, or tip amount.
Work inside the parentheses first (that's the percent of the price), then subtract or add as shown.
Row 1: compute 0.20 × 45 first. Then subtract that amount from 45 to get the sale price.
onLevel.explanation: Each Calculation column already shows the setup, so compute the parentheses first and then subtract or add. Row 1: 0.20 × 45 = 9, so the sale price is 45 − 9 = $36. Row 2: 0.08 × 60 = 4.80, so the total is 60 + 4.80 = $64.80. Row 3: 0.15 × 25 = 3.75, so the total is 25 + 3.75 = $28.75. Discounts subtract; tax and tips add.
onLevel.explanationEs: La columna "Calculation" ya muestra el planteamiento, así que calcula primero lo que está entre paréntesis y luego resta o suma. Fila 1: 0.20 × 45 = 9, así que el precio de oferta es 45 − 9 = $36. Fila 2: 0.08 × 60 = 4.80, así que el total es 60 + 4.80 = $64.80. Fila 3: 0.15 × 25 = 3.75, así que el total es 25 + 3.75 = $28.75. Los descuentos restan; el impuesto y las propinas suman.

onLevel.stem: A store marks up a $30 item by 40%, then a customer gets 10% off. What is the final price?
choiceFeedback: First add the markup, then subtract the discount from that price.
Do this in two steps: markup first, then the discount.
Make sure you're applying the discount to the marked-up price.
hints: This is a TWO-step problem: the markup happens first, and the 10% discount applies to the marked-up price — not the original $30.
Step 1: raise $30 by 40%. Step 2: take 10% off that new price.
Start with the markup: $30 × 1.40 = $42. Now find 10% of $42 and subtract it from $42.
onLevel.stemEs: Una tienda aumenta el precio de un artículo de $30 en un 40% y luego un cliente recibe un 10% de descuento. ¿Cuál es el precio final?

onLevel.instructions: A $80 pair of shoes is 25% off. Use the bar model to show the discount and sale price.
onLevel.label: 25% of $80 = $20 discount. You pay 75% = $60.
hints: The bar splits $80 into two pieces: the 25% you save and the 75% you still pay.
25% is one-fourth, so the discount piece = the whole divided by 4. The rest is what you pay.
Divide $80 by 4 to get the discount piece. Then subtract it from $80 to see the 'You pay' piece.
onLevel.explanation: The bar splits the $80 into the 25% you save and the 75% you still pay. Since 25% is one fourth, the discount piece is 80 ÷ 4 = $20, leaving 80 − 20 = $60 as the sale price. That $60 is also 0.75 × 80, which is why the second piece of the bar is labeled 75%.
onLevel.explanationEs: El modelo divide los $80 en el 25 % que ahorras y el 75 % que sí pagas. Como 25 % es una cuarta parte, la pieza del descuento es 80 ÷ 4 = $20, y quedan 80 − 20 = $60 como precio de oferta. Esos $60 también son 0.75 × 80, y por eso la segunda pieza del modelo dice 75 %.

onLevel.stem: A restaurant bill is $35. You want to leave a 20% tip. What is the total amount you pay?
choiceFeedback: Multiply $35 by 0.20 to find the tip.
Find 20% of $35.
Check: what is 20% of $35?
hints: The question asks the TOTAL you pay — the bill AND the tip together, not just the tip.
Find 20% of $35 first, then add it onto the $35 bill.
Compute the tip: 0.20 × 35 (or take 10% of 35 and double it). Then add it to $35.
onLevel.stemEs: La cuenta de un restaurante es de $35. Quieres dejar una propina del 20%. ¿Cuál es la cantidad total que pagas?

onLevel.title: Spot the Discount-then-Tax Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: A $50 jacket is 20% off, then 5% tax is added. Find the final price.

workedExample.label: Find the discount and sale price
workedExample.work: 0.20 × 50 = 10 off, so the sale price is 50 − 10 = $40.

onLevel.correctWork: Tax goes on the price you actually pay ($40), not the original $50. Tax = 0.05 × 40 = $2. Final price = 40 + 2 = $42.
hints: After the discount you pay $40, not $50. Which price should the tax be based on?
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de descuento y luego impuesto
onLevel.explanation: The "Add the tax" step charges the 5% on the original $50 instead of on the $40 you actually pay after the discount. Tax is always applied to the current price, so the tax is 0.05 × 40 = $2 and the final price is 40 + 2 = $42, not $42.50.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Add the tax" cobra el 5 % sobre los $50 originales en lugar de sobre los $40 que realmente pagas después del descuento. El impuesto siempre se aplica al precio vigente, así que el impuesto es 0.05 × 40 = $2 y el precio final es 40 + 2 = $42, no $42.50.

extending.title: Find the Discount Error

workedExample.label: A prize costs 160 tickets at 25% off. Find the sale price.

hints: The student forgot to convert the percent to a decimal before multiplying.
25% = 0.25. Multiply 0.25 × 160 = 40 ticket discount. Final: 160 − 40 = 120 tickets.
extending.explanation: The "Find 25% of 160" step multiplies by 25 instead of by 0.25, which is 100 times too big. Rewrite the percent as a decimal first: 25% = 0.25, so the discount is 0.25 × 160 = 40 tickets and the sale price is 160 − 40 = 120 tickets. A negative sale price is a signal that the percent was never converted.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Find 25% of 160" multiplica por 25 en lugar de por 0.25, lo que da un resultado 100 veces más grande. Convierte primero el porcentaje en decimal: 25 % = 0.25, así que el descuento es 0.25 × 160 = 40 boletos y el precio de oferta es 160 − 40 = 120 boletos. Un precio de oferta negativo es la señal de que nunca se convirtió el porcentaje.

extending.prompt: A store has a 20% off sale, then takes an additional 10% off the sale price. Is this the same as 30% off the original? Use $100 as the original price. Show your work for both scenarios and explain the difference.
extending.sentenceFrame: Taking 20% off then 10% off gives a final price of $___, but 30% off the original gives $___. The difference is $___ because ___.
extending.hint: Calculate the final price by applying the first discount, then applying the second discount to that result.
hints: The trap: the second discount (10%) is taken from the SALE price, which is smaller than $100 — so it saves less than $10.
Run both scenarios with $100: (a) 20% off then 10% off the result; (b) 30% off all at once. Compare the finals.
Scenario (a) step 1: 20% off $100 leaves $80. Now find 10% of $80 — not of $100 — and subtract it from $80.
extending.explanation: The two paths do not match. Taking 20% off $100 leaves $80, and then 10% off $80 is only $8, so the final price is $72. Taking 30% off $100 at once removes $30 and leaves $70. The stacked discounts save $2 less because the second percent is applied to the smaller $80 base, not to the original $100.
extending.explanationEs: Los dos caminos no dan lo mismo. Quitar 20 % de $100 deja $80, y luego 10 % de $80 es solo $8, así que el precio final es $72. Quitar 30 % de $100 de una vez resta $30 y deja $70. Los descuentos encadenados ahorran $2 menos porque el segundo porcentaje se aplica a la base más pequeña de $80, no a los $100 originales.
extending.promptEs: Una tienda tiene una rebaja del 20%, y después descuenta un 10% adicional sobre el precio rebajado. ¿Es lo mismo que un 30% de descuento sobre el precio original? Usa $100 como precio original. Muestra tu trabajo en los dos casos y explica la diferencia.

extending.instructions: You are shopping at the arcade prize store. Calculate the final price for each item after discount AND 6% tax.
hints: Follow the finished Headphones row: discount first, THEN the 6% tax is charged on the discounted price.
For each item: price − discount = After Discount. Then 0.06 × (After Discount) = tax. Add them for the final.
Speaker: 15% of $80 is 0.15 × 80 = $12 off, so After Discount = $80 − $12. Then take 6% of that number for the tax.
extending.explanation: Follow the finished Headphones row: discount first, then tax on the discounted price. Speaker: 0.15 × 80 = $12 off, so After Discount is $68; 0.06 × 68 = $4.08 tax, so the Final Price is $72.08. Game: 0.40 × 25 = $10 off, so After Discount is $15; 0.06 × 15 = $0.90 tax, so the Final Price is $15.90.
extending.explanationEs: Sigue la fila terminada de "Headphones": primero el descuento y luego el impuesto sobre el precio ya rebajado. Bocina: 0.15 × 80 = $12 de descuento, así que "After Discount" es $68; 0.06 × 68 = $4.08 de impuesto, así que el precio final es $72.08. Juego: 0.40 × 25 = $10 de descuento, así que "After Discount" es $15; 0.06 × 15 = $0.90 de impuesto, así que el precio final es $15.90.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Use Percent to Solve Problems is combining the discount and tax into one single percent change instead of applying them one after another. For a $40 item with a 25% discount and 8% sales tax, a student might compute 40 × (1 − 0.25 + 0.08) = 40 × 0.83 = $33.20, treating the tax as if it applies to the original price. But tax is charged on the discounted price, not the original price: first take 25% off $40 to get $40 × 0.75 = $30, then add 8% tax on that $30: $30 × 1.08 = $32.40. The correct final price is $32.40, not $33.20 — always compute the discount first, then apply tax to the new lower price.
